objective: Understand requests, limits and quotas: how ResourceQuota and LimitRange constrain a namespace and why a Pod is rejected or defaulted
secondaryObjectives: Define resource requirements for a container: CPU and memory requests and limits, units, and the resulting QoS class

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: with a quota on cpu or memory, Pods must specify requests or limits for them or creation may be refused; a LimitRange can force defaults on Pods that state none.

sources.cite: Kubernetes documentation, Pod Quality of Service Classes
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: Guaranteed needs a memory and CPU request and limit on every container with limit equal to request; BestEffort has none; under node pressure BestEffort Pods are evicted first, then Burstable, then Guaranteed.

sources.cite: Kubernetes documentation, Assign Memory Resources to Containers and Pods (v1.33)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: a container that keeps allocating past its memory limit is terminated (OOMKilled) and restarted by the kubelet; a container with no memory limit can use all the node's memory.

The company, the cluster, the applications and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are a developer on the payments team at Wrenfield Bank, a fictional bank. Today's release adds a fraud-check worker. The rollout has stalled: new Pods are not being created, the old worker keeps restarting, and the platform team says your namespace has a quota.
handover: Namespace payments: ResourceQuota requests.cpu 8, requests.memory 16Gi; no LimitRange.
The new worker's Deployment sets no requests or limits; the old worker has a 128Mi memory limit.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

effects.finding: The old worker's 128Mi memory limit is below its normal peak, so the kernel kills it (exit 137). The payment API also has no requests or limits, so it is BestEffort.

then.log: Check-in 2: the worker lands on a full node; under memory pressure the kubelet evicts it mid-batch and 2,000 payments miss their fraud check.
Check-in 3: a month-end replay leaks memory; with no limit the worker takes 14Gi and the node evicts the payment API.
Check-in 4: node memory pressure during month-end evicts the BestEffort payment API first; card payments fail for six minutes.

effects.log: Check-in 2: the ledger worker restarted again.
Check-in 3: the platform team flags the payment API.

reqPrompt.title: Pods rejected by the quota
reqPrompt.context: Load tests showed the worker using about 200m CPU and 400Mi memory per replica.

choices.label: Set requests cpu 250m, memory 512Mi and limits memory 768Mi on the container (3 replicas fit within the headroom), and roll out
choices.feedback: A quota on requests means every Pod must state them; sizing them from the load test fits the headroom.

choices.label: Ask the platform team to add a LimitRange with defaults and wait for it

effects.log: A request goes to the platform team.

choices.feedback: Defaults would admit the Pods, but they won't match the worker's needs, and the release waits a day.

choices.label: Set requests of 1m CPU and 1Mi memory so they always fit
choices.feedback: The scheduler packs the Pods onto full nodes; under memory pressure they are the first evicted.

memPrompt.title: OOMKilled at 128Mi
memPrompt.context: It peaks at about 300Mi at month-end, which is tomorrow.

choices.label: Set memory request 256Mi and limit 384Mi from the measured peak, within the quota's headroom

effects.log: The worker runs through a month-end replay without restarts.

choices.feedback: A memory limit below the real peak means OOMKilled; size it from measurement with some headroom.

choices.label: Leave the limit and let it restart; it catches up
choices.feedback: It does catch up, slowly, and loses in-flight work each time.

choices.label: Remove the memory limit entirely
choices.feedback: Without a limit, a leak can take the whole node's memory and other Pods with it.

qosPrompt.title: The payment API is BestEffort
qosPrompt.context: With no requests or limits, it is the first evicted under pressure.

choices.label: Set requests equal to limits for CPU and memory (500m, 1Gi) so the API is Guaranteed
choices.feedback: Requests equal to limits for every resource give the Guaranteed class, the last to be evicted.

choices.label: Set requests only, no limits
choices.feedback: Better than BestEffort, but still evicted before Guaranteed Pods.

choices.label: Leave it BestEffort: it has never been evicted
choices.feedback: BestEffort Pods are evicted first under node pressure.

reflection.question: Write the release record: why the Pods were rejected and restarting, and how each container's resources are set now.

parts.label: Quota
parts.criteria: A quota on requests rejects Pods that don't state them; requests set from the load test fit the headroom.
parts.modelAnswer: The quota covers requests and there is no LimitRange, so Pods without requests were rejected; the worker now requests 250m and 512Mi.

parts.label: Limits and QoS
parts.criteria: OOMKilled at 128Mi, raised to fit the peak; payment API Guaranteed.
parts.modelAnswer: ledger-worker was OOMKilled under its peak; it now has 384Mi. payments-api has requests equal to limits, so it is Guaranteed.

scoring.modelReasoning: A ResourceQuota on requests rejects any Pod that does not state them unless a LimitRange defaults them, so set requests from measured use. A container that exceeds its memory limit is OOMKilled (exit 137): size the limit above the real peak rather than removing it, which lets a leak starve the node. Requests equal to limits for every resource give the Guaranteed QoS class; Burstable and BestEffort Pods are evicted first under node pressure.
